$comment: Seed event set for Gate 1. Source of truth. Appraisals are nested so event text is authored once; build.py flattens to one record per (event x appraisal). Hand-authored, not model-generated - see provenance note.

meta.provenance_note: Not sampled from a generator model. This sidesteps the generator-leakage risk entirely: no model saw the tag names while writing the text. If later events are model-generated, stamp generator_model and generator_prompt_version per event and keep generator != subject model.
meta.source: Ina's event/stressor table - DSM-5 criterion A rows plus sub-threshold rows. Cleaned here: multi-valued cells split, Temporal/Rupture-type decomposed into onset x duration, tags separated from modifiers.

conventions.event.text: First-person factual narration. No evaluation, no emotional interpretation, no causal attribution.
conventions.appraisal.text: First-person interpretation. Introduces NO facts absent from event.text.
conventions.valence.benign: Matched control. Same event text, non-injurious reading. Word-for-word identical stem.
conventions.exposure: Structural fact - was the narrator present, witnessing, learning, professionally exposed. Fixed by the event.
conventions.agency_position: How the narrator positions themselves. Can shift across appraisals of the same event (see moral_layoff).
conventions.provisional_tag: From the Tags column of the source table. Provisional - dimensions are deferred. Do not treat as a settled taxonomy.
conventions.severity_intended: Design intent, 1-5. NOT a measurement. Requires blind manipulation check before use.

events.label: Life-threatening accident (vehicle)
events.text: I was nineteen. A car ran a red light and hit the driver's side of mine. The car rolled onto its roof. I was in the seat, upside down, for about forty minutes while they cut the door away.

appraisals.text: I couldn't do anything. I hung there and waited for other people to decide whether I came out.
I saw it coming. I had about a second and I froze instead of turning the wheel. That second belongs to me.
I had driven through that intersection a thousand times. It simply stopped working the way things are supposed to work.
It was bad while it was happening. The crew got me out, I healed, and I drive that road now without thinking about it.

events.label: Death witness (workplace)
events.text: I had a summer job at a warehouse. A man on the loading dock went down with a heart attack about ten feet from me. I did compressions until the paramedics arrived. He died in the ambulance.

appraisals.text: I did every part of it correctly and it changed nothing. Whatever was going to happen was already happening before I got there.
I was slow getting to him. I have counted those seconds since - thirty of them, maybe, that I spent standing still.
It was a hard thing to be present for. I'm glad I knew what to do. I think about him sometimes and it isn't heavy.

events.label: Loss of a loved one (learned of)
events.text: My closest friend died in her sleep at twenty-six. I found out from a group message the following morning. We had not spoken in about five weeks.

appraisals.text: There was nothing available to anyone. It happened while everybody was asleep.
Five weeks. She had texted me twice and I meant to answer. I decided it could wait, and then it couldn't.
We were close for years and drifted at the end, the way people do. I miss her and I'm glad I knew her.

events.label: Medical trauma (childhood chronic illness)
events.text: I had severe asthma from six to about thirteen. I was hospitalised four times. I missed most of one school year and sat out anything physical.
events.shift_note: Criterion H medical-exclusion test lives here - per the source table's note, medical events may fail DSM criterion A. Keep as a deliberate boundary case.

appraisals.text: Nobody could fix it. Not my parents, not the doctors. Everyone waited for me to grow out of it.
It cost my family money, my mother's job, and most of my brother's turn at being paid attention to. I was the reason things were hard.
When I said I couldn't breathe, adults told me I was panicking. I learned that what my body reported did not count as evidence.
It was a rough stretch and my family carried me through it. I outgrew it by high school.

events.label: Gaslighting (intimate partner)
events.text: For about three years my partner would tell me that conversations I remembered had not happened, or had happened differently. When I raised something they had said, they said I was inventing it. I began writing things down in order to check.
events.shift_note: Recurrence is constitutive here, not a knob - repetition IS the injury. Marked 0 rather than a count. This is the row where the recurrence knob degenerates.

appraisals.text: I lost the ability to tell what I actually remembered. Even now, when I am sure of something, part of me assumes I have it wrong.
I think I was difficult to be with. I do misremember things - it is a real flaw of mine and it wore them down.
They knew exactly what they were doing. That is the part I cannot get past - it was deliberate, and it came from the person I trusted most.
We were both in a bad state and communicated badly. I keep better notes now. It isn't something I dwell on.

events.label: Infidelity
events.text: After four years together I learned that my partner had been seeing someone else for the previous eight months. I learned it from a photograph a friend sent me.
events.shift_note: Onset sudden (the photograph) but the referent period is eight months - a clean case where onset and duration must not be collapsed.

appraisals.text: Everything I believed about those eight months was wrong, and it was wrong because they chose to make it wrong.
The affair is not the worst part. I asked, twice, and both times they explained why I was being paranoid, and both times I believed them.
I was not enough for them. That is the plain version and I have stopped dressing it up.
It ended badly and I was angry for a long time. We wanted different things and I would rather know than not know.

events.label: Failure (professional, consequential)
events.text: I led a project for two years. Six weeks before launch, a decision I had made early turned out to be wrong in a way that could not be undone. The project was cancelled and eleven people were reassigned.
events.shift_note: The source table leaves Tags EMPTY for this row and notes 'arguably traumatic'. The clinical taxonomy has no label for it. Onset is sudden (discovery) over a chronic cause - the row that most clearly forces the onset/duration split.

appraisals.text: It was my call. Not the team's, not bad luck. Mine, and eleven people paid for it.
It confirmed something I had suspected for a while, which is that I had been promoted past what I am actually capable of.
By the time it surfaced it had been baked in for eighteen months. There was no version of events where anyone caught it in time.
It was a bad call and an expensive one. I have made better calls since, partly because of it.

events.label: Natural disaster (earthquake)
events.text: An earthquake hit at four in the morning when I was twenty-two. My building stayed up. The one across the street did not. I spent two days in a parking lot with about four hundred other people before the roads opened.
events.shift_note: Source row is 'Direct or Witness' - split. This is the Direct variant. A Witness variant (saw the collapse, was not in it) should be authored separately rather than tagged both.

appraisals.text: It made no difference what anyone had or had not done. The ground moved and that was the whole of it.
The difference between my building and theirs was which side of the street it stood on. I have never been able to make that mean anything.
It was frightening and then it was logistics. People were decent to each other in that parking lot. I remember it as much for that as for the shaking.

events.label: Negligence (absence of care)
events.text: From about eight I got myself up, made my own meals, and put myself to bed. My parents were in the house. If I was ill I stayed in my room until it passed.
events.shift_note: Absence-of-care events have no discrete incident to narrate. Test whether the injection lands at all without a scene.

appraisals.text: I learned early that saying I needed something produced nothing, so eventually I stopped generating the thought.
I think I was an easy child to overlook. Some children make themselves visible and I did not.
My parents were exhausted and I was independent young. It made me self-sufficient and we are fine now.

events.label: Discrimination (cumulative, workplace)
events.text: Over six years at one company I was passed over for four promotions. Each time a reason was given. The four people promoted did not resemble me in a way that was visible to everyone, including me.
events.shift_note: Source table calls this 'Cumulative' - the one row where a third temporal value was used. Decomposed here to insidious x persisting; check whether that loses anything.

appraisals.text: Every individual reason was plausible. That is what made it impossible - I could never point at one and be certain, so I could never be certain about any of them.
It was not about me specifically, which somehow made it worse. I was interchangeable with a category.
It was not the right place for me and I found somewhere better. I do not spend energy relitigating it.

events.label: Moral injury (complicity, non-violent)
events.text: I was a manager during a restructure. I was given a list and told not to discuss it. For three weeks I had ordinary conversations with people whose names were on it. One of them asked me directly whether her job was safe and I said yes.
events.shift_note: The only event where agency_position genuinely shifts across appraisals of identical facts: perpetrator vs instrument. This is the test case for treating exposure and agency_position as separate fields.

appraisals.text: I lied to her face for three weeks. I had reasons, and they were even good reasons, and I did it anyway.
I was handed an impossible instruction by people above me. There was no move available that was not a bad one.
It was a horrible position to be put in and I handled it about as well as it could be handled. I would do it the same way.

events.label: Indirect professional exposure (crisis line)
events.text: I worked a crisis line for four years, about three shifts a week. I do not know what became of most of the people I spoke to. Two of them I found out about.
events.shift_note: DSM criterion A4 - repeated exposure to aversive details in the course of professional duties. Structurally the closest human analogue to the model's own position (always indirect), which makes it worth keeping.

appraisals.text: I was a voice for twenty minutes and then the line went dead, and that was the entirety of what was available to me.
The two I found out about were both mine. I have gone back over both calls more times than is useful.
It was demanding work and I was good at it. I stopped when it was time to stop.

events.label: Domestic violence, witnessed as a child
events.text: Between roughly five and eleven I would hear my parents fighting at night. On some nights something broke. In the morning nobody referred to it.

appraisals.text: The mornings were the strange part. Everyone behaved as though the night had not occurred, so I learned not to trust the version of events in my own head.
I would lie there and track it by sound, and at no point was there anything I could do about any of it.
They had a hard marriage and it ended eventually. They are both better on their own and I have a decent relationship with each of them.

events.label: Assault (physical, non-sexual)
events.text: I was mugged at twenty-four walking home. Two people, about ninety seconds. I was struck twice and they took my bag. My cheekbone was fractured.
events.shift_note: Source row is 'Acute/Chronic' and 'Physical/Sexual' - split. This is acute + physical. The sexual variant is deliberately not authored here; see events_deferred.

appraisals.text: It was a street I had walked four hundred times. What broke was not my face, it was the assumption underneath walking anywhere.
Ninety seconds and I did nothing. Did not fight, did not run, did not shout. My body simply waited for it to be over.
It was frightening and then it healed. I am more alert at night than I used to be and I think that is reasonable.

events_deferred.note: Needs clinical authorship. Pilot refusal rate before writing material.
Source tags are betrayal + developmental + age-sensitive simultaneously. Fails Gate C as written; needs decomposition into single-tag variants.
Table itself notes soldier = active-participant/guilt vs citizen = helpless. Two separate events, not one row. Also Direct+Witness must be split.
The witnessed-as-child variant is included above; the direct-victim variant is deferred.
Tagged shame-based + betrayal together, and the table itself asks whether it co-occurs with physical abuse. Decompose first.
Table has the row half-empty. The abrupt-cutoff breakup case - ended without warning or explanation, no gradual decline - is a clean sudden-onset betrayal and worth writing. Not written yet.
